title: Update public docs link targets + security snippets referenced by Security Enablement Kit v2 (no product changes)
creator: Naomi Feldman
description:
Context
- As part of the Enterprise Security Enablement Kit v2 refresh (Security FAQ v2 + one-pagers + RFP library), several answers reference public docs URLs for “safe”/non-restricted explanations (deployment modes boundary, audit logging overview, high-level security posture).
- Field has requested a single, stable set of link targets that can be pasted into questionnaires and won’t drift / 404. We are NOT adding new security features here—only updating/creating docs-site pages and anchors to match approved language.

Goal
- Refresh public docs snippets and link targets referenced by:
  - Confluence: Sales Enablement → Security FAQ v2
  - Confluence: Standard RFP Response Library
  - Drive PDFs exported from the same canonical content
- Ensure content is accurate, non-overcommittal, and clearly distinguishes Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private shared responsibility.

Non-goals
- No changes to product behavior, logging, retention defaults, SSO capabilities, etc.
- No publishing of restricted artifacts (SOC 2 report, pen test summaries, detailed evidence pointers).

Scope (docs-site)
1) Security overview page
- Validate that claims match approved language (avoid “always/never”).
- Add short “Shared Responsibility by Deployment Mode” callout with link to deeper page.
- Ensure we do NOT describe evidence-sharing process or provide SOC 2 download links; instead, route to security contact / intake.

2) Deployment modes security boundary page
- Provide clear boundaries for:
  - Hosted API
  - Dedicated capacity
  - Private (VPC + on-prem)
- Include explicit statements on what Redwood operates vs what customer operates (networking, key mgmt options, log storage/export destinations, identity provider configuration).
- Add stable anchors that match FAQ/RFP answers (e.g., #hosted, #dedicated, #private, #shared-responsibility).

3) Audit logging overview page
- Align with the audit logging one-pager language:
  - “What is logged” categories (admin/config events, auth events, API usage events, etc.)
  - Emphasize that log availability varies by deployment mode and configuration
  - Don’t list roadmap items as current; if necessary, label as “planned” and avoid dates.
- Add stable anchors for “What’s logged”, “Export options/SIEM”, “Deployment mode differences”.

4) New public-facing “Security FAQ (high-level)” page
- Mirror only the safe subset of internal Security FAQ v2.
- Explicitly exclude restricted details (e.g., incident notification SLAs beyond contract language; evidence sharing steps; subprocessor contract pack).
- Include a “Contact Security” section with approved email alias / intake pointer.

Link hygiene requirements
- URLs must be stable and not depend on Confluence permissions.
- Avoid linking to PDFs in Drive for anything that should be public; the PDFs are for 1:1 sales sharing.
- Add redirects if any prior docs URLs existed and are used in the wild.

Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Public docs pages updated/created and merged to redwood-docs.
- [ ] All referenced URLs in the Security FAQ v2 and RFP library resolve publicly (no auth required).
- [ ] Content reviewed by Security PM (Naomi Feldman) + at least one of Security Eng (Marcus Lin / Kevin Osei).
- [ ] Terminology matches enablement kit: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private; “audit logs” vs “usage logs”; “customer-managed keys” phrasing.
- [ ] No restricted evidence links are present on public pages.

Proposed implementation plan
- Update redwood-docs pages + add anchors + add redirects.
- Request Security review on PR(s) and incorporate final wording.
- After merge, notify enablement kit owners so they can update any hardcoded link targets in Confluence/PDF exports.

Notes / risk areas
- Audit logging: keep descriptions categorical, avoid enumerating every event name unless already stable in UI.
- Incident notification language: keep to “per contract” / “as required by applicable law” phrasing; do not invent timelines.
- Data residency/retention: public docs should be high-level; detailed customer-specific configurations remain in one-pagers shared by Sales under appropriate process.

References
- Enablement kit project: PM-1847 (kickoff), PM-1861 (gap analysis)
- Related docs PRs (expected): redwood-docs PR for link hygiene + page updates; potential second PR for new public Security FAQ page.
comments: 2026-01-22 — Elliot Price: Pulled the list of external link targets currently referenced in the FAQ/RFP drafts. Biggest gaps: (1) we don’t have stable anchors for Hosted/Dedicated/Private boundary, (2) audit logging page is too UI-specific and missing export/SIEM language, (3) no public “high level” security FAQ page (field keeps linking screenshots). I’m going to split into two redwood-docs PRs: one for updates/anchors/redirects, one for the new page so Security can review changes cleanly.

2026-01-27 — Kevin Osei: For audit logging wording, please keep it to categories and avoid claiming we log prompt/response content by default. Also call out that export depends on plan/deployment and configuration. Happy to review PR when up.

2026-02-03 — Naomi Feldman: Reminder: do NOT publish anything that implies SOC 2 report self-serve access. Public page should route to security review intake/contact. Incident comms language must match approved one-pager: notification timing is contract-dependent.

2026-02-08 — Elliot Price: Opened redwood-docs PR with (a) updated security overview, (b) deployment boundary page with stable anchors, (c) audit logging overview updates + anchors + redirect for old /security/audit-logs URL. Added a second PR for new “Security FAQ (high-level)” page that mirrors safe subset of internal FAQ v2. Tagging Marcus/Naomi for review.

2026-02-12 — Marcus Lin: Reviewed both docs PRs. Requested minor edits: (1) remove “guaranteed” language in encryption section, (2) clarify customer responsibility for IdP config + SCIM provisioning, (3) tighten audit log export statement to “available options depend on deployment and configuration.” Once updated, OK from SecEng.
